sweepFindings.quote: ch22: "Asher's phone lights the bedroom before his feet touch the floor." / ch22: "Does it sleep outside the bedroom, or does it wake the mind before the feet hit the floor?" / ch23: "you wake after four hours of sleep... The hand reaches for sugar" + q07 "you value peace, yet your phone wakes you before your feet touch the floor" / ch25: "a person can look ordered and still be ruled by bad sleep, crowded rooms, late snacks, and a phone that keeps the nerves lit" / ch26: "Qing reaches for her phone before the kettle clicks off... If she chooses from scratch, the loudest request gets the first hour."
sweepFindings.detail: The identical 'phone is the first object reached for in the morning and it hijacks the day before your feet hit the floor' opening scene is reused as the central illustrative frame across four consecutive chapters. ch22 (Asher), ch23 (the four-hours-sleep waker / q07), and ch26 (Qing) all stage the same wake-up-and-grab-the-phone tableau, and a reader moving chapter to chapter would feel the same scene reset with a new name each time. This is the single most repeated scene skeleton in the batch.

sweepFindings.quote: ch22: "shoes by the door, phone outside the room, table cleared before sleep" and "Set the notebook on the chair. Place the shoes by the door... Clear the table before you quit for the night." / ch23: "a real bedtime alarm, one cleared corner of the desk" / ch25: "Put the shoes where you will see them" / "set your walking shoes beside the door" / ch26: "A chair, a calendar square, a pair of shoes by the door" / "shoes by the door"
sweepFindings.detail: The exact environment-prep triad — shoes by the door, phone out of the room, clear the table/desk — is recycled as the concrete 'action' payload of four chapters' practices (Train the Next Default ch22, Body Ally Check ch23, Clear a Walking Route ch25, Anchor the Day First ch26). The same three props in the same phrasing carry four supposedly distinct skills, so the implementation plans read as copy-paste of one another.

sweepFindings.quote: ch23 (Severin): "Severin has forty minutes before the board call and a blank calendar square... He budgets ten minutes for a walk, ten for one hard slide, five for water... No work begins yet; the choice is the work." / ch25 (Weston): "Weston has 40 open minutes before the supplier review locks. The calendar offers three claims on that space: polish slides, answer small messages, or reserve a quiet walk... He blocks the 40 minutes" / ch24 (Benoit): budget memo declining a program before "the board packet closes"
sweepFindings.detail: The 'protagonist has ~40 spare minutes before a board/supplier review and must choose to spend it polishing slides vs. protecting the body/walk' planning_choice scene is duplicated almost beat-for-beat in ch23 (Severin) and ch25 (Weston): same 40-minute window, same 'polish slides vs. protect body' fork, same 'the choice is the work' resolution. Different nouns (board call vs. supplier review), identical frame.

sweepFindings.quote: ch19 (Deepak): "By Thursday morning, Deepak's listening session has already failed... answered Rachel after nine seconds." / ch22 (Lawrence): "Lawrence is halfway through a rehab clinic meeting when he hears himself praising Stoicism... he snaps at a late question." / ch24 (Brigitte): "Brigitte is typing, 'Happy to help'... Halfway through the sentence, she sees the two hidden days behind that cheerful yes." / ch26 (Minh): "Minh is halfway through the wellness kickoff when he hears himself make Fred Rogers's 143 pounds sound like a medal... stops mid-sentence" / ch20 (Janet): "her reply has already turned one sloppy report into a trial of the report writer's character"
sweepFindings.detail: The 'protagonist is mid-action (teaching/typing/speaking), HEARS HIMSELF contradict the very lesson, and corrects in real time' mistake_recovery skeleton is the default failure-scene across five chapters: Deepak (ch19), Lawrence (ch22), Brigitte (ch24), Minh (ch26), Janet (ch20). The 'halfway through... hears himself... and corrects' construction is near-verbatim in ch22, ch24, and ch26. A reader sees the same self-catch beat recycled as the postmortem/mistake_recovery example in chapter after chapter.

sweepFindings.quote: ch20 (Nancy/Hailey): "Nancy and Hailey receive the same forwarded complaint... Nancy drafts a reply... leaves it through lunch... Hailey sends her version from the break room before the coffee cools." / ch22 (Aryan/Mathias): "Aryan and Mathias both leave the courthouse after a tense hearing with one hour before bed. Aryan keeps his phone in hand... Mathias puts the phone in the hall... walks ten quiet blocks." / ch24 (Zoe/Lane): "Zoe and Lane receive the same investor request... Zoe... removes two shiny features. Lane accepts both... Zoe ships a clearer release; Lane's team spends Friday explaining"
sweepFindings.detail: The 'two named people meet the identical provocation/request; one applies the lesson and wins, one doesn't and pays by Friday' contrast skeleton is reused three times: Nancy/Hailey (ch20), Aryan/Mathias (ch22), Zoe/Lane (ch24). Same structure: same stimulus to both, virtuous one vs. impulsive one, diverging outcome stamped to a later time (lunch / morning / Friday).

sweepFindings.quote: ch20 tryThisNow: "Block 10 minutes tomorrow at 8:30 at your desk for a hot-letter review; use the first face-heating message as the trigger." / ch22 tryThisNow: "Before you leave this screen, change one setting or surface..." / ch23 tryThisNow: "Create a 12-minute body check on tomorrow's calendar at 8:15 a.m. in your kitchen, triggered by pouring coffee" / ch26 tryThisNow: "Put a 12-minute reset on tomorrow's calendar for 8:15 a.m. at your kitchen table, triggered by opening your inbox."
sweepFindings.detail: The tryThisNow openers share one rigid template: '[N]-minute [practice] on tomorrow's calendar at [8:1x/8:30 a.m.] in your kitchen/desk, triggered by [coffee/inbox].' ch23 and ch26 are almost identical (12-minute, 8:15 a.m., kitchen, triggered by a morning cue). This is more than a pedagogical convention — the same clock time, same room, and same trigger-grammar are stamped across chapters.

sweepFindings.quote: ch24 card05: "Earlier concept, Limit Your Inputs: how does saying no support that discipline?" / ch25 card05: "How does protective refusal help a real walk happen?" / ch26 card04: "How does the earlier Say No boundary protect a routine?" / ch26 card05: "How does the earlier Take a Walk practice belong inside a routine?" / ch22 card04: "How does interconnection from All Is One change a body routine?" / ch23 card04: "Spaced recall, Limit Your Inputs..." card05: "Spaced recall, Enough..."
sweepFindings.detail: Each chapter dedicates 1-2 review cards to a near-identical 'Earlier concept, [Prior Chapter Title]: how does it support [this chapter]?' callback card. The phrasing template ('Earlier concept, X' / 'Spaced recall, X' / 'How does the earlier X...') is mechanically reused as a fixed card slot across at least five chapters, producing structurally interchangeable cards 04/05 in every chapter.

sweepFindings.quote: ch22 weeklyPractice: "For seven days, run Train the Next Default each night: reset one surface for morning, move one distraction away..." / ch23 weeklyPractice: "For seven days, keep a three-line log..." / ch26 weeklyPractice: "For seven days, run a two-minute evening review: mark the anchor kept, moved, or missed..." / ch24 weeklyPractice: "For seven days, review three accepted requests..." / ch25 weeklyPractice: "For seven days, protect one unfilled walking route."
sweepFindings.detail: Every weeklyPractice in this batch opens with the identical 'For seven days, [log/run/protect]...' formula and resolves to a nightly/evening review-and-mark ritual. ch22, ch23, and ch26 all reduce to 'each night, reset/log/review one thing and mark whether it held' — the same seven-day-evening-log shape wearing different labels, which a reader doing the workbook would notice as the same assignment repeated.

sweepFindings.quote: ch21 (Hamza laundry room): "Hamza kneels in the laundry room under a buzzing light. Blue lint clings to his cuff... Hamza pulls the lint free, folds the towels to one side, and leaves the room easier for the next person." / ch23 (Hugo/Theophile bus thread) and ch23 broader 'copy the famous routine but skip the support' frame; ch21 'Chantal can stand under a huge Earthrise print, say that all people are one, and still snap at the guard'
sweepFindings.detail: Lower-confidence: the 'tired person in a mundane shared/ordinary space performs one small humble act that proves the abstract idea has become conduct' vignette frame recurs (Hamza's laundry room in ch21; the 'ordinary route / one cleared corner' humility move in ch23/ch25). Weaker than the others because the surface details differ, but the 'the lesson is measured by one small unglamorous act nobody forced' beat is a shared authorial reflex.

sweepFindings.quote: ch23 ex05/q06 (Theophile as owner): "Theophile expects the late-night trainee to win Saturday's timing test at the fencing school... Theophile checks the video." and "At Theophile's Japan fencing school, a trainee quotes Miyamoto Musashi" / ch23 ex06 (Theophile as remote mentor texting Hugo): "Hugo texts Theophile from the bus... Theophile: Eat, nap 20, then ten clean swings."
sweepFindings.detail: Within ch23, 'Theophile' is used as two different characters: in ex05/q06 he is the owner/instructor of a Japan fencing school running a timing test, while in ex06 he is a peer mentor whom Hugo (a youth-sports student) texts from a bus for swing advice. The fencing-school proprietor and the texting buddy do not read as the same person, so the shared name causes persona drift inside the chapter. (Cross-chapter name reuse across ch19-26 is otherwise well-isolated.)
